chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a man divorces his wife while he is in a state where there is no return (raj'ah) to her, she does not inherit him, nor does he inherit her."
And he said: "He inherits and is inherited as long as the blood has not appeared from the third menstruation, if he has the right of return (raj'ah) to her."

key_terms.صَحِيح: Sound/valid (referring to the state of the divorce)

ai.seo_question: When does a divorced wife stop inheriting from her husband during the waiting period?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the specific temporal marker for the finalization of a revocable divorce (talaq raj'i), establishing that the husband retains inheritance rights until the wife completes her third menstrual cycle post-divorce. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the 'iddah' period as a time of continued marital bond, distinguishing it from the irrevocable divorce where inheritance ceases immediately. The hadith provides a practical legal criterion for determining the exact moment when the 'right of return' (haq al-raj'a) and corresponding inheritance rights terminate.
